correctness.rationale: For fixed R>0 and a real C² mean-zero h, the polar boundary r²<R+εh preserves area πR exactly. At the disk the Fock monomial e_0 has isolated top eigenvalue 1−e^(−R), gaps e^(−R) S_m(R). The coherent-state projector integral is trace-norm C² for compact bounded boundary motion, so simple-eigenvalue perturbation is legitimate. The second derivative is −e^(−R)||h||²+2e^(−R)Σ_{m≥1}(R^m/m!)/S_m |hhat_m|². Real Parseval eliminates mean mode, cancels m=1 and yields the claimed Φ_m=S_(m−1)/S_m Hessian coefficient. S_m/(R^m/m!) is strictly increasing in integer m, giving the sharp Φ_2=2/(R+2) inequality and equality directions. Falling factorial term domination for m/R→α<1 and initial partial-sum divergence for α≥1 give min(α,1), including ∞. Independent numerical Fock matrix angular quadrature at R=1 cos2 converges to e^(−1)/6=0.061313240195; 12×12 top-eigenvalue matrices at ε=0.1,0.05,0.025,0.0125 gave 0.0613839252,0.0613308989,0.0613176541,0.0613143436. Finite matrices are normalization checks, not infinite proofs.

The very relevant Ramos (2026) manuscript computes first variations and second-harmonic geometric separation, and the 2024 Gómez–Guerra–Ramos–Tilli work computes second variation for an optimized-superlevel functional, rather than the same λ_max(D_ε) operator. No implication yielding Φ_m found on reading these relevant sections; unindexed equivalence risk remains.

Computing all angular directions produces a sharp eigenvalue stability constant and a nontrivial large-area frequency crossover m≈R, not merely rewriting the global Faber–Krahn bound. Pure m=2 gives optimal transverse second-order loss and higher modes quantify shape sensitivity.
